proseChanges.summary: The owner's paths became files upstream never overwrites rather than files an update never touches, and the owner's agent may adapt them while landing one.
proseChanges.was: `src/ext/`, `.seed/`, `migrations/ext/`, and `tests/local/` were the owner's, and updates never touched them.
proseChanges.now: `src/ext/`, `.seed/`, `migrations/ext/`, and `tests/local/` are the owner's; upstream releases never overwrite them, and the owner's agent may adapt them during an update.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Your agent may change your own files as part of landing a release — adapting an extension to a changed core API rather than working around it. Upstream still never commits to those paths.

proseChanges.summary: `pnpm verify` runs the owner's override replacement tests and local intent tests as part of the run, rather than reporting them separately from the contract.
proseChanges.was: `pnpm verify` reported the contract as satisfied, overridden, or broken, and reported your intent tests separately.
proseChanges.now: `pnpm verify` reports the contract as satisfied, overridden, or broken and runs each declared override replacement test and each local intent test in the same run.
proseChanges.ownerAction: A `replacementTest` named in `src/ext/contract-overrides.json` and every test under `tests/local/` must pass for `pnpm verify` to be green; a replacement test that has stopped running is now a failure rather than a separate report.

proseChanges.summary: The update candidate became a starting point rather than a result to accept or reject: how the change lands is the owner's call.
proseChanges.was: `rer update` fetched the latest verified tag, rebased the owner's commits, ran migrations and `pnpm verify`, then offered the candidate; on failure it reported the conflicting files, the affected clauses from `RELEASE.json`, and the relevant `.seed/intent.md` lines. Resolution meant working that candidate until `pnpm verify` passed, and nothing named intent as the thing an update had to preserve.
proseChanges.now: `rer update` prepares a candidate with the owner's commits on top, runs migrations and `pnpm verify`, then offers it as a starting point; how the update lands is the owner's call. On a conflict it stops and reports the conflicting files, the affected clauses from `RELEASE.json`, and the relevant `.seed/intent.md` lines. Whatever route the agent takes, every requirement in `.seed/intent.md` is preserved unless the owner changes it, and `pnpm verify` — including declared override replacements and local intent tests — passes before adopting.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Your agent chooses how an upstream release comes in: take the candidate, re-derive it, or land the change another way. The verified outcome is what counts, and a conflict is your agent's work rather than a reason to defer the update.

proseChanges.summary: The seed now states its licence in the repository instead of leaving it to the marketplace listing.
proseChanges.now: MIT, in `LICENSE` at the root of the installation, covering the code the owner receives and everything they build on it.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Nothing to do. Keep the file when you fork or rename the installation.

agentUpdateInstructions: No clause changed meaning in this release, so `contractChanges` is empty and adopting it moves no guarantee: what changed is what the owner-facing documents promise. Three of those positions are now yours to rely on. Files under `src/ext/`, `.seed/`, `migrations/ext/`, and `tests/local/` are still never overwritten by upstream, and you may adapt them while landing an update instead of working around them. `pnpm verify` runs each declared override replacement test and each local intent test, so a green run covers them and a replacement test that no longer runs is a failure. Preserve every requirement in `.seed/intent.md` unless the owner changes it, and treat the update candidate as a starting point rather than a result to accept or reject.
